title: Synthesis route-dependent structural and electrochemical properties of La 0.63 Ga 0.37 Mo 0.74 Fe 0.26 O 3−δ  symmetrical electrodes for intermediate-temperature SOFCs
content: This study carefully explores the impact of synthesis route on the structural, optical and electrochemical properties of La0.63Ga0.37Mo0.74Fe0.26O3−δ (LGMF) as a symmetrical electrode for intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells (IT-SOFCs). The LGMF material was synthesized via four distinct routes such as sol–gel, hydrothermal, co-precipitation and solid-state methods. The detailed characterization of the prepared materials revealed strong dependence of phase formation route, crystallinity and band gap. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Raman spectra confirmed the formation of crystalline perovskite-related phases, with the co-precipitation and sol gel routes exhibiting improved crystallinity and structural homogeneity. UV-visible analysis shows a gradual reduction in band gap, narrowing from 2.26 eV to 1.93 eV indicating enhanced defect concentration and charge transport characteristics. Among all synthesis routes the co-precipitation method exhibits the lowest ohmic resistance as 0.44 Ω and the highest total conductivity of 0.70 S cm−1 at 650 °C (operating temperature). Consequently, fuel cell testing reveals that the co-precipitation-synthesized electrode has the highest fuel cell performance with a peak power density of 286 mW cm−2. The results prove that the co-precipitation method offers a suitable approach for preparing high-performance and redox-stable symmetrical electrodes for IT-SOFCs by improving electrocatalytic activity and ionic/electronic transport properties.
